project.name: SociaLite chat media and reply recovery

why: An official Android sample turns a chat thread into a compact media workflow: capture from the conversation, edit a captured video, return to the thread, and recover an asynchronous reply through a notification when the app is closed. It is a useful reference for preserving conversational context while moving through transient media tools.
taskGoal: Send text or captured media in a chat, make a lightweight video edit when needed, and receive a reply even after leaving the app.

screens.purpose: Choose an existing conversation from the list of chat threads.
screens.evidence: The official README identifies a Chat List Screen containing the app's chat threads.

screens.purpose: Compose text or media messages while retaining the active conversation context.
screens.evidence: The README describes the Chat Screen as an individual message thread that sends text and media.

screens.purpose: Capture a photo or video without abandoning the message task.
screens.evidence: The README states that the camera icon in the Chat Screen opens an in-app camera for photos and videos.

screens.purpose: Make a minor edit after recording a video, before returning to the conversation flow.
screens.evidence: The README names a Video Edit Screen for minor edits after a video is captured in the in-app camera.

screens.purpose: Restore awareness of an asynchronous reply after the user has closed the app.
screens.evidence: The README says an avatar replies after five seconds and, with notification permission, the reply is notified when the app is closed.

screens.purpose: Reach a bounded recovery control for resetting chat history.
screens.evidence: The README identifies a Settings Screen for tasks including resetting chat history.

transitions.contract: Select a thread before composing so each media action has an explicit conversational destination.
Launch capture from the active thread instead of making the user reconstruct the recipient after creating media.
Offer video editing only after a video capture, keeping the capture path lighter for other media.
Return edited media to the original thread so sending remains a continuation of the same task.
Use notification permission to preserve reply awareness when the conversation is no longer foregrounded.

platformConstraints: The closed-app reply notification depends on notification permission being granted.
The media path distinguishes in-app capture from selecting existing media through the Android photo picker.
The sample's AI chat configuration requires separately configured Firebase and Gemini Developer API services; it is not assumed to be available in the basic chat flow.

exceptionStates.scenario: The user closes the app before the asynchronous reply arrives.
exceptionStates.recovery: Notify the reply when notification permission is available, rather than requiring the user to keep the thread open.

exceptionStates.scenario: The user wants to correct or abandon their conversation history.
exceptionStates.recovery: Expose the history-reset action in Settings as a deliberate, bounded recovery path rather than mixing it into normal message composition.

exceptionStates.scenario: Media capture creates a video that needs adjustment before sending.
exceptionStates.recovery: Route captured videos through the dedicated edit screen and return to the originating chat thread afterward.

capture.attribution: The Android Open Source Project; SociaLite sample maintained in the official android/socialite repository.
capture.reusePolicy: inspiration-only — record the documented mobile flow and recovery behavior in an original abstract preview. Do not copy SociaLite screenshots, animal avatars, media, names, marks, or bundled third-party assets. The source code is Apache-2.0, but third-party components retain their own notices.
